primary_goal: Get the visitor to start a SPIEGEL+ digital subscription trial ('4 Wochen für 1 €') to unlock the article

friction_points.issue: The paywall appears right after the headline, teaser and hero image. No article text is shown, so the visitor is asked to pay before seeing any value from the piece.
friction_points.evidence: Below the teaser 'Der Linken-Parteitag machte den Weg frei…' and the photo caption, the next element is the 'Jetzt Artikel freischalten:' box. No body paragraph is visible.

friction_points.issue: The two offers use different price units, so they are hard to compare. The cost after the trial is only implied by a struck reference price.
friction_points.evidence: Option 1: '4 Wochen für 1 €, statt 20,95 €'. Option 2: '12 Wochen für 2,99 € pro Woche, statt 4,99 €'. One is priced per period and the other per week. Neither shows the price after the offer ends next to the CTA.

friction_points.issue: Low-quality, clickbait ads placed directly under the paywall undermine the premium positioning the visitor is being asked to pay for. The same ad also appears twice in a row.
friction_points.evidence: Two identical 'Unglaublicher Ansturm auf Mini-Hörgeräte: Dieses unsichtbare Hörgerät verkauft sonst keiner' ads are stacked immediately below the paywall and the 'Startseite' link.

friction_points.issue: Large empty black areas, probably unfilled ad slots, create long dead scroll zones. The page looks broken and pushes 'Mehr lesen über' and the related content far down.
friction_points.evidence: There are several tall empty blocks: between the small 4-up ad row and the Renault/Hurtigruten/Abarth sponsored block, after the Abarth ad, and before 'SPIEGEL Games'.

friction_points.issue: A display ad sits above the headline, so the editorial content and the paywall start lower in the first viewport.
friction_points.evidence: An 'ANZEIGE' donation banner ('Spende für das Projekt…', 'Spendenziel') appears between the breadcrumb and the 'Rot-Grün-Rot' kicker.

friction_points.issue: The sticky DER SPIEGEL header is rendered in the middle of the page and overlaps the hero image.
friction_points.evidence: The orange 'DER SPIEGEL' bar with 'Anmelden' cuts across the top of the photo of Krach, Eralp and Graf, below the 'SPIEGEL bei Google bevorzugen' link.

friction_points.issue: The secondary links for existing subscribers are small and low-contrast. Print subscribers, a high-intent segment, may miss the discounted upgrade path.
friction_points.evidence: 'Sie haben bereits ein Digital-Abo? Hier anmelden' and 'Sie haben bereits ein Print-Abo? Hier vergünstigt Digital-Zugang bestellen' appear in small grey text at the bottom of the paywall box.

friction_points.issue: No payment-method cues are shown near the CTA. German users often look for PayPal or direct debit before starting a subscription.
friction_points.evidence: The paywall box shows only the price options, three benefit bullets and 'Jetzt für 1 € testen'. There are no PayPal, SEPA or invoice badges.

hypotheses.hypothesis: If the post-trial price and cancellation terms are stated directly under the CTA, then trial starts will improve because visitors won't hesitate over hidden follow-on costs.
hypotheses.change: Add a line under 'Jetzt für 1 € testen': 'Danach 20,95 € / 4 Wochen. Jederzeit online kündbar.'
hypotheses.primary_metric: paywall conversion rate (trial starts / paywall views)

hypotheses.hypothesis: If the first 1–2 paragraphs are shown before the paywall, then trial starts will improve because readers will be invested in the story when they are asked to pay.
hypotheses.change: Show the first 1–2 body paragraphs with a fade-out above the paywall box

hypotheses.hypothesis: If both offers use the same price unit and show the saving, then selection and conversion will improve because the choice becomes a simple comparison.
hypotheses.change: Express both offers per week (e.g. '0,25 €/Woche für 4 Wochen' vs '2,99 €/Woche, 40% günstiger') or both per period, and add a savings badge
hypotheses.primary_metric: paywall conversion rate; revenue per paywall view

hypotheses.hypothesis: If PayPal and SEPA badges are shown under the CTA, then trial starts will improve because payment friction and trust concerns drop.
hypotheses.change: Add small PayPal / Lastschrift / Kreditkarte icons below the primary CTA

hypotheses.hypothesis: If the duplicate clickbait ads directly below the paywall are removed or moved further down, then paywall conversion will improve because premium perception stays intact around the purchase moment.
hypotheses.change: Deduplicate the 'Mini-Hörgeräte' ad and enforce an ad-free buffer of about one viewport below the paywall

quick_wins: Collapse unfilled ad slots so empty black areas take no height
Increase contrast and size of the 'Hier anmelden' and Print-Abo upgrade links
Add a one-line post-trial price and cancellation note under the CTA
Mark the 12-week option with a savings badge so the second offer has a clear reason to exist
uncertainties: Whether the mid-page sticky header and the empty black areas are real rendering issues or artifacts of the full-page screenshot
Whether the post-trial price is disclosed after clicking the CTA (in the checkout step)
Which payment methods are offered at checkout
Whether a body text preview is shown to some users (e.g. metered or referral traffic) and hidden only in this session
Desktop layout, since only a mobile view is visible
Ad revenue trade-off: removing or moving ads near the paywall may cost display revenue, which the test should measure
Small text (caption, bullet details, footer) is not fully legible at this resolution
